correctness.rationale: For a marked pair, rank at least one means the four orientations to the pair all occur. Rank at least three of the empty marking therefore requires a vertex admitting such a pair with both an in-neighbor and an out-neighbor. Fewer than six vertices cannot realize even one full pair profile; at six, the two witnesses force the same vertex's outdegree to be 2 and 3, respectively. Rank at least four requires a triple with eight distinct possible extensions, hence at least eleven vertices. A separately written and executed bottom-up recursion scans every labelled tournament of orders 1–7. It finds no rank-three case below seven and 1,503,216 positive cases at seven. Exact orbit enumeration gives 313 of 456 classes and the positive automorphism-order counts (1:292, 3:17, 5:2, 7:1, 21:1), with labelled counts recovered from orbit weights. By the rank-four obstruction all positive cases at seven have rank exactly three.
residual_risks: The census classifies automorphism-group orders, not permutation actions or general higher-order group structure.
No cutoff at rank four or census beyond seven vertices is claimed.

value.rationale: This is the natural first nontrivial host-order cutoff for the specified extension depth, not an arbitrary slice. The census shows that the first possible order already has many distinct qualifying hosts, and the orbit refinement quantifies how automorphisms affect the comparison between labelled and unlabelled prevalence. It supplies an exact reference point for later structural work on the invariant.
residual_risks: The result is a finite classification by rank and group order, not a structural theorem for arbitrary tournaments.
